kaigo-depth-team-handoff.heading: Connect specific information and questions with the multidisciplinary team
paragraphs: Multidisciplinary cooperation is more than learning job titles. Start with the life the person wants, situations causing difficulty and what was actually observed, then specify what advice is needed. ‘Please refer to a professional’ alone may not convey necessary information.

Physical therapists mainly address basic movement; occupational therapists address daily activities; speech-language therapists address language, communication and swallowing difficulties, among other areas. One daily-life difficulty may involve several disciplines. Rather than assigning everything to one person based on a title, check responsibilities and consultation contacts.

Care workers report events during meals and activities, the person’s own words and changes from usual. Separate successful and difficult parts and the conditions in which difficulty arose so the recipient can understand. If the cause or diagnosis is unconfirmed, keep it unconfirmed.

Sending a report, its receipt, confirming advice and changing a support plan are separate events. Ask about unclear explanations and confirm who will provide which support and what may be changed before implementing it.

Keep personal wishes central and share necessary information with necessary recipients within the needed scope. This learning organizes roles and consultation content. It does not instruct care workers to diagnose, design rehabilitation exercises independently or change food textures or drinks based only on a report.

Learning case: Kai wants to join club activities but finds arranging objects by hand and speaking before a group difficult. A worker sends only ‘Please ask PT to handle everything.’ Separate participation wishes, observed difficulties and desired support checks, then organize responsibilities and consultation contacts. The cause of speaking difficulty is not yet diagnosed.

kaigo-depth-observation-evidence.heading: Record personal words, observations and measurements separately
paragraphs: Make sources clear to readers. Personal sensations and wishes, actions workers actually observed and measured values complement each other. Do not turn a report of tiredness into a temperature value or diagnose from appearance alone.

When noticing a change, specifically record known times, circumstances and observations during that period. Observation time differs from whether the condition began earlier. Do not add unknown periods or unobserved areas as though confirmed.

If values are unavailable, state that no measurement was taken. A worker feeling hot, measuring room temperature and measuring the person’s body temperature are separate. Avoid turning an impression or action into an established cause.

Records of near misses or hazards should lead to necessary reporting and follow-up checks. No injury does not mean no remaining hazard. Instead of blaming the person or staff before establishing cause, review environment, equipment and methods as a team.

If an unsupported conclusion is already recorded, correct it using facility methods so the change is identifiable. This teaches observation and measurement, not diagnostic or treatment thresholds. In urgent conditions, do not wait for polished writing before seeking help or making contact.

Learning case: at 14:00,Lien says ‘I feel tired today’ and stops folding towels twice. No measurements were taken, but the record says ‘fever due to a hot room.’ Preserve time, words and actions, correct the unconfirmed fever and cause conclusions, and report the change to the person responsible.

kaigo-completeness-hand-choice.heading: Check hand-hygiene methods and completion
paragraphs: Before hand hygiene, check visible dirt, recent contact and the next task. Washing with water and soap differs from rubbing in an alcohol product. Do not choose solely for convenience, such as proximity or speed.

For visible dirt, wash with running water and soap. Cover necessary surfaces of both hands, including backs, between fingers, thumbs, fingertips and nail areas, not palms alone. Check facility rules for rings and watches; counting actions alone does not establish adequate washing.

After soap washing, check through rinsing under running water and suitable drying. For hand rubbing, use the product-specified amount and method to cover areas and rub until dry. Do not finish by wiping the product away with paper before drying.
Even clean hands can be contaminated again by a dirty towel or surface. Check new contacts before the next task and perform hand hygiene at necessary times. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.

This unit teaches method differences, surfaces, completion and transition to the next task. Amounts, duration and product/pathogen-specific choices follow facility infection precautions, product instructions and workplace training. Do not derive improvised procedures from the text.

Learning case: after collecting soiled towels, visible dirt remains on the hands. Colleagues suggest hurried hand rubbing or gloves alone. Choose water and soap based on visible dirt, and check surfaces, rinsing, drying and possible renewed contamination before the next task.

kaigo-completeness-worker-capacity.heading: Check your condition and task requirements first
paragraphs: Reducing back strain requires checking personal abilities, workspace, equipment, staffing and responsibilities as well as posture. Feet apart alone does not establish a safe single-worker transfer. Before accepting a task, check whether the method suits the person and worker.

If you have back pain, fatigue or another condition making safe work difficult, tell the person responsible. Hiding pain and relying on force may increase risks for both worker and resident. Current worker health informs review of support conditions too.

Choose lifts, slide sheets and similar equipment suited to the person and task, check condition before use and use trained methods. Equipment in storage does not establish understanding of that model or agreed teamwork responsibilities.

Also report lack of training on equipment. Confirm who will operate it, under which plan and with which supporters. For someone needing full assistance, consider lifts or other methods that avoid relying on manual lifting.

This explanation teaches consultation and checks before work, not techniques for lifting, pulling, moving someone or placing a fulcrum against the body. Individual assessment, equipment instructions and workplace training are needed. Do not try an unclear method alone.

Learning case: the worker has back pain today and has not trained on the stored slide-sheet model. Asked to reposition someone, they must not assume feasibility from posture and equipment presence alone. Report and check their condition, training, the individual plan and helper responsibilities.

kaigo-completeness-drill-followup.heading: Track responsibilities and rechecking outcomes after drills
paragraphs: Disaster preparedness includes more than supplies: usable routes, communication methods, who supports whom and how each person receives information also matter. A fully stocked bag does not establish that assigned help can reach someone needing it.

Drills test whether plans work and reveal difficulties. Failed contact or unusable routes should be recorded separately from attendance numbers. Everyone being present does not establish safe completion.

If gaps are found, follow facility plans to confirm what remains incomplete, whom it was reported to and who accepted responsibility. A name on a roster differs from actual acceptance of this response. Do not invent an unconfirmed substitute or route.

Confirm responsibility for correction and when and how effectiveness will be checked. Separate actions such as clearing items or calling again from verified outcomes such as usable routes, received information or connected support. Use findings in later drills and plan reviews.

This teaches preparedness checks and reporting, not one evacuation sequence for every earthquake, fire, storm or flood. In real emergencies, follow trained facility responses and instructions rather than waiting to finish a learning report.

Learning case: drill bags contain the required supplies, but the assigned supporter for someone needing hearing assistance cannot be contacted, and a cart blocks the planned route. Report checked supplies separately from unfinished communication and route issues, and confirm response and rechecking responsibilities under the facility plan.

kaigo-completeness-emotion-confirm.heading: Do not infer feelings or motivation from expression alone
paragraphs: Expressions and behavior offer cues for asking the person. Silence alone does not establish sadness, anger or unwillingness to participate. Ask without leading the answer and check current feelings and wishes.

Willingness to join differs from conditions making participation difficult. Noise, hunger, fatigue, anxiety and other factors may overlap. Record confirmed words and observations rather than explaining every response through one imagined cause.

Supporting motivation can include preserving small meaningful choices: participation format, songs, topics, and when or with whom to spend time. Discuss available choices and actual conditions. Activity counts or staff praise do not prove personal satisfaction.
Consider support according to confirmed wishes, separating abilities from conditions not yet checked. A wish for time alone must not become a claim that all future interaction is refused.

Needs models and expressions do not diagnose psychological conditions or establish decision-making ability. Respect feelings and discuss support according to the individual plan. Give specific information to the necessary responsible person if difficulties or changes persist, for example.

Learning case: during music time, the person speaks little and looks toward the door. When asked, they say, ‘The room is noisy, so I want to listen alone. I want to choose the songs.’ Separate observation from their words and discuss listening conditions without replacing them with assumptions of disliking interaction or lacking motivation.

kaigo-completeness-memory-transfer.heading: Separate familiar skills from memory for new information
paragraphs: Memory includes encoding new information, retaining it and recalling it when needed. One successful or unsuccessful task does not establish every process.

Distinguish semantic memory for knowledge such as word meanings, episodic memory for experiences such as when someone was met, and procedural memory for learned skills. Performing a familiar task well does not establish that a newly heard schedule was remembered.

If the person cannot answer about newly provided information, first check whether it was conveyed through an accessible method and whether content and question were understood. Do not decide it is solely memory without checking conditions such as hearing in a busy room.

Record observed skills, replies, explanation conditions and unconfirmed parts separately. Discuss short explanations, quiet locations or usable communication methods, and check what was understood and remembered within that task’s scope.

This teaches concepts and information gathering. One forgotten schedule does not diagnose disease, and one familiar skill does not guarantee entirely normal memory. This material does not replace dementia testing or assessment of decision-making ability.

Learning case: the person folds towels skillfully in a familiar way but cannot state an activity time just given in a busy room. Do not infer all memory is normal from the skill. Also check whether the message was heard and understood; one reply alone does not establish disease.

169.title: Connect specific information and questions with the multidisciplinary team
objectives: Create handovers including wishes, observations and specific consultation questions.
Do not treat a professional’s name alone as a completed response or plan change.
169.context: Learning case: Kai wants to join club activities but finds arranging objects by hand and speaking before a group difficult. A worker sends only ‘Please ask PT to handle everything.’ Separate participation wishes, observed difficulties and desired support checks, then organize responsibilities and consultation contacts. The cause of speaking difficulty is not yet diagnosed.
169.artCaption: Discuss daily-life information, such as eating, with several responsible people around the person. The picture does not identify professions or advice by appearance alone.

170.title: Record personal words, observations and measurements separately
objectives: Separate personal words, actions and measurements by information source.
Correct assumed causes and connect with risk reporting and checks.
170.context: Learning case: at 14:00,Lien says ‘I feel tired today’ and stops folding towels twice. No measurements were taken, but the record says ‘fever due to a hot room.’ Preserve time, words and actions, correct the unconfirmed fever and cause conclusions, and report the change to the person responsible.
170.artCaption: Workers check records together. Separate the person’s own words, observations and actual measurements.

171.title: Check hand-hygiene methods and completion
objectives: Distinguish hand-hygiene methods according to visible dirt and task.
Check surfaces, drying, renewed contamination and the limits of gloves.
171.context: Learning case: after collecting soiled towels, visible dirt remains on the hands. Colleagues suggest hurried hand rubbing or gloves alone. Choose water and soap based on visible dirt, and check surfaces, rinsing, drying and possible renewed contamination before the next task.
171.artCaption: Left shows drying after washing; right shows rubbing in a product. Distinguish washing from hand rubbing. This picture alone does not establish completion of every stage.

172.title: Check your condition and task requirements first
objectives: Report back pain or training gaps as support conditions.
Separate equipment presence from readiness to handle it safely.
172.context: Learning case: the worker has back pain today and has not trained on the stored slide-sheet model. Asked to reposition someone, they must not assume feasibility from posture and equipment presence alone. Report and check their condition, training, the individual plan and helper responsibilities.
172.artCaption: Check plans and task conditions around an empty bed. The picture does not show a technique for lifting someone alone.

173.title: Track responsibilities and rechecking outcomes after drills
objectives: Distinguish unfinished supplies, communication, routes and assigned support.
Track acceptance of responsibility separately from verified effectiveness.
173.context: Learning case: drill bags contain the required supplies, but the assigned supporter for someone needing hearing assistance cannot be contacted, and a cart blocks the planned route. Report checked supplies separately from unfinished communication and route issues, and confirm response and rechecking responsibilities under the facility plan.
173.artCaption: Consider worker health and disaster supplies. Checking a bag alone does not complete contact or route checks.

174.title: Do not infer feelings or motivation from expression alone
objectives: Do not infer feelings from expression or silence alone.
Ask participation wishes separately from environmental difficulties.
174.context: Learning case: during music time, the person speaks little and looks toward the door. When asked, they say, ‘The room is noisy, so I want to listen alone. I want to choose the songs.’ Separate observation from their words and discuss listening conditions without replacing them with assumptions of disliking interaction or lacking motivation.
174.artCaption: Listen to concerns. Expression alone does not establish feelings or participation wishes.

175.title: Separate familiar skills from memory for new information
objectives: Distinguish skill, knowledge and experience-related memories.
Check hearing and understanding rather than judging all functions from one result.
175.context: Learning case: the person folds towels skillfully in a familiar way but cannot state an activity time just given in a busy room. Do not infer all memory is normal from the skill. Also check whether the message was heard and understood; one reply alone does not establish disease.
175.artCaption: A scene involving familiar button use and photographs. One skill or picture cannot diagnose all memory functions.

weekly-kaigo-depth-team-handoff-probe.prompt: How should ‘Please ask PT to handle everything’ be revised in this case?
options: Report participation wishes, specific difficulties arranging objects and speaking to groups, observations and consultation questions; clarify responsibilities and relevant contacts.
Keep only PT as the recipient, omitting wishes and daily-life details.
Report only arranging objects and dismiss speaking difficulty as unrelated.
Treat the plan as already changed after sending and start new exercises without checking.
rationales: This gives daily-life goals and specifics and discusses relevant expertise with the responsible person. It does not diagnose speaking difficulty or assume one profession solves everything.
A job title alone does not convey the support needed or personal goal.
This dismisses several participation-related difficulties without grounds.
Sending differs from confirming a changed plan and does not authorize independently designing exercises.
weekly-kaigo-depth-team-handoff-probe.reading: Practice case: Kai wants to join club activities. Arranging objects by hand and speaking before a group are difficult. The worker sent only ‘Please ask PT to handle everything.’ Causes and a new support plan remain unconfirmed.

weekly-kaigo-depth-observation-evidence-.prompt: Which correction and handover matches the facts about Lien?
options: Retain confirmed fever because the worker felt hot.
Delete reported tiredness and two interruptions because no temperature value exists.
Record room heat as the certain cause because towel folding stopped twice.
Preserve the 14:00 words, two interruptions and absent measurements separately; correct unsupported fever/cause using facility methods and report the change.
rationales: Worker sensation differs from measured body temperature; unmeasured fever cannot be established.
Personal words and observed actions remain valuable without measurements and should be retained separately.
Actions alone do not determine cause; other conditions remain unconfirmed.

This separates time, subjective information, observations and uncertainty. Use facility correction methods rather than erasing history without authorization, and communicate information for assessment.
weekly-kaigo-depth-observation-evidence-.reading: Practice case: at 14:00,Lien said ‘I feel tired today’ and stopped towel folding twice. No temperature or other measurements were taken. The record says ‘fever due to a hot room.’

weekly-kaigo-completeness-hand-choice-pr.prompt: With visible dirt on the hands, what is appropriate before the next task?
options: Choose only the nearest product location, ignoring dirt and the next task.
Wash with water and soap, checking both hands’ surfaces, rinsing and drying; do not rely on gloves, and watch for renewed contamination.
Record only rubbing counts without checking surface coverage.
Treat all later contact as needing no checks because hands were initially cleaned.
rationales: Convenience alone cannot decide: check visible dirt and task content.
Visible dirt requires washing. Consider areas, completion and later contacts without substituting gloves for hand hygiene.
Counts alone do not prove coverage of thumbs, fingertips or other areas.
Dirty contact can recontaminate hands. Check new contacts and necessary timing.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-hand-choice-pr.reading: Practice case: after collecting soiled towels, visible dirt remains on the hands. Clean-supply containers will be handled next. Colleagues suggest ‘rub in the product quickly’ or ‘gloves alone are enough next.’

weekly-kaigo-completeness-worker-capacit.prompt: You have back pain and are untrained on the stored equipment model. What should you report and check before acting?
options: Report pain and training gaps; check the person’s plan, suitable equipment, operators, teamwork responsibilities and preparation.
Feet-apart posture is enough, so do not report pain or lack of training.
Record training and device checks as complete when equipment is found in storage.
Check only personal abilities; worker condition and helper roles are unnecessary.
rationales: Evaluate worker health and competence together with the person and task conditions. Posture or equipment presence alone does not establish readiness.
Posture alone does not determine strain. Hiding pain or training information prevents appropriate support arrangements.
Equipment presence differs from usable preparation or model knowledge.
Worker, environment, equipment and teamwork are safety conditions as well as the person’s abilities.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-worker-capacit.reading: Practice case: the worker has back pain today and is asked to reposition someone. A slide sheet is in storage, but they have not trained on this model. A colleague says correct standing posture is enough.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-drill-followup.prompt: The drill bag is checked, but the supporter is not reached and a cart blocks the route. What recording and follow-up is appropriate?
options: Treat contact and route as checked and the drill complete because supplies are ready.
Treat responsibility as accepted despite no reply because the name is on the roster.
Separate checked supplies from unfinished contact and route issues; confirm response responsibility and rechecking through the facility plan.
Treat assigning cart removal as already rechecking a usable route.
rationales: Stocked supplies do not establish received information or a usable route.
Roster responsibilities differ from actual contact and acceptance.
This identifies achievements and remaining problems and follows correction through effectiveness checks, without inventing substitutes or routes.
Assignment, correction and verification of effect are separate stages.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-drill-followup.reading: Practice case: disaster-drill bag contents are checked. The assigned supporter for someone needing hearing assistance has not been reached. A cart makes the planned route impassable.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-emotion-confir.prompt: After checking wishes during music time, which record matches the case?
options: Little speech establishes refusal of all future interaction.
Separate observed little speech and looking at the door from the wish to listen alone because of noise and choose songs, and discuss listening conditions.
Wanting to listen alone also means no wish to choose songs.
Many planned activities establish satisfaction and participation wishes.
rationales: This expands one observation into rejection of all future interaction.
This preserves confirmed feelings and choice without replacing them with assumptions or diagnoses of disliking interaction or lacking motivation.
The person explicitly wants to choose songs. Do not cancel that part of the wish.
Activity counts do not replace checking satisfaction and wishes.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-emotion-confir.reading: Practice case: during group music time, the person speaks little and looks at the door. The worker initially assumes dislike of interaction. Asked directly, the person says, ‘The room is noisy, so I want to listen alone. I want to choose the songs.’

weekly-kaigo-completeness-memory-transfe.prompt: The person folds towels well but cannot state the activity time just given. Which understanding is appropriate?
options: The familiar skill establishes entirely normal memory for new information.
Record disease from one missed answer without checking whether the explanation was heard.
A busy room establishes noise as the certain cause.
Separate the successful skill from the unanswered information; check whether the message was received and understood, and communicate accessibly.
rationales: Skill observation does not guarantee encoding, retention or recall of new information.
Check hearing and comprehension conditions; one reply does not establish diagnosis.
Noise is a condition to check, but actual hearing difficulty remains unconfirmed.
This separates memory and information-reception processes without guaranteeing all memory from one skill or diagnosing disease from one lapse.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-memory-transfe.reading: Practice case: the person folds towels skillfully using a familiar method, but cannot state an activity time just given in a busy room. The worker assumes all memory is normal because towel folding is possible.
